title: Safehouse and Drop
premise: Ulyana Hartwell, a crash investigator whose family died in row twelve, discovers the accident was a live test of a voice-cloning network trained on stolen grief recordings — including her own late husband's. Following a voiceprint unlock to a server farm abroad, she infiltrates the operation with help from a defected engineer and his ragtag crew of test subjects who've become her found family. In a race against the border checkpoint shift change, she burns the training archive, exposing the network and reclaiming her own voice as inheritance rather than loss.
about_author: Silas Ashgrove is the pen name of a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade reconstructing black-box audio before turning to fiction. They write from a farmhouse where, they insist, every phone call is recorded by no one.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Two years after the crash, Ulyana replays the recovered cabin audio nightly until she hears something impossible: her husband's voice saying words he never spoke. Tracing the anomaly to a data broker's leak, she realizes victims' voices were harvested as training material. The emotional beat is grief curdling into purpose — she stops mourning and starts investigating.

chapters.title: The Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with interludes from Marek, a guilt-ridden engineer inside the network. Her husband's cloned voiceprint unlocks a dead-drop server in Riga, pulling her overseas. Marek, disgusted by what he built, defects and offers her shelter among former test subjects — strangers bound by stolen voices who adopt her without ceremony. Beat: wary trust becoming tentative belonging.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating Ulyana and Marek POVs. The crew plans to breach the server farm and burn the training archive before the 3 a.m. checkpoint shift change, when new biometric scanners go live. A betrayal within the group forces them to move early; Ulyana must choose between the archive and Marek's capture. Beat: terror sharpened by loyalty — she finally has people worth losing.

chapters.title: What the Dead Would Say
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Inside the burning facility, Ulyana confronts the network's architect, who offers her a perfect reconstruction of her family's voices. She refuses, destroys the master model, and escapes across the border in the shift-change gap with Marek and the crew. Epilogue: she sleeps through the night for the first time, her own voice — not theirs — carrying forward. Beat: release and chosen inheritance.
